items.title: Data-Driven Heuristic-Guided Business Process Redesign
items.abstract: Business process redesign (BPR) has a long-standing catalog of best-practice redesign heuristics, yet, applying them remains a mostly manual task that requires extensive domain knowledge. Despite recent advances using Large Language Models (LLMs) for conversational process model redesign, limitations remain. For example, redesign is user-driven instead of data-driven and is not guided by best practices such as the redesign heuristics. Moreover, only one change can be handled at a time. To address these limitations, given an event log and a BPMN model, we present the DH-BPR framework to realize data-driven heuristic-guided BPR using LLMs. To design DH-BPR, we first conducted an analysis of which redesign heuristics can be automatically detected and applied given information contained in an event log such as the fraction of cases that bypass an activity. Based on this, DH-BPR detects and validates heuristic candidates through a combination of rule-based techniques and an LLM. After that, DH-BPR jointly designs and records an application plan for valid candidates, before finally yielding a redesigned BPMN model and an updated resource model (the way resources execute the process). Evaluation based on simulation using a synthetic benchmark and two real-world event logs shows that the framework's redesign reduces the mean case completion time by up to 61.5%.

items.title: Decomposing the Associative Chain: Schema-Based Mediation Supports Expression and Understanding in Human-AI Music Co-creation
items.abstract: Users cannot reliably translate their creative intents into AI-generated music. We contend that the root of this difficulty lies in associative divergence: associations between narratives and musical features are overly remote, and users lack a visible mediation structure to negotiate them. To address this, we introduce five core schema groups as cognitive mediation and propose a bidirectional schema-based framework. Its forward pathway decomposes narrative-to-music associations into staged mappings, while its reverse pathway provides structured interpretations from music back to narrative. Findings from two user studies(N = 188; N = 60) show that the framework led to clearer creative expression and greater perceived control, improved the comprehensibility of generated music, especially for unconventional pieces. Furthermore, it supported cultural and affective thinking while helping users locate associative divergence. Our work points toward better creative intent alignment in human-AI music co-creation.

items.title: Design Practices for Public Algorithmic Systems: Grounded in Technocratic and Businesslike Logics
items.abstract: Algorithmic and AI systems employed in public administration often manifest technocratic and efficiency premises which may conflict with the democratic and socio-technical fundaments of algorithmic practices in government. Partially, these premises are infused into these public algorithmic systems during the design process. This paper conducts a case study in a consortium of Dutch public organisations that reshapes design practices of algorithmic systems to uncover institutional logics underlying these practices. Our observations and interviews at the consortium of 13 public organisations revealed four design practices that deviate from sociotechnical design practices: (1) distance from politics, (2) underrate the input from non-technical experts, (3) operate on a procurement-oriented dynamic, and (4) follow a chronological phasing combined with agile or scrum practices. Through abductive reasoning, we derived the technocratic and businesslike logics that shaped these design practices. These institutional logics clash with the socio-technical, political, and material nature of public algorithmic systems. To arrive at more responsible, accountable and ethical use of these systems in government, public organisations need to modify their design practices. Our findings provide initial insights into the institutional logics required to change design practices, while also underscoring the complexity of altering routines and practices that are deeply rooted in organisational structures and cultures.

items.title: Design, Implementation, and Performance Evaluation of an AI-Driven Security Operations Center (AI-SOC) for Complex Enterprise Network Environments: Assessing the Role of Human Factors and Quality Management in Cyber Resilience
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital transformation and complex network infrastructures has increased the sophistication and scale of cyber threats, challenging the effectiveness of traditional defense mechanisms. Traditional security operations centers (SOCs) often struggle to meet modern cybersecurity requirements because of their reactive structures, siloed toolkits, and over-reliance on manual processes. Many existing artificial intelligence (AI)-driven SOC (AI-SOC) studies emphasize simulation-based evaluations and seldom analyze the impact of human factors on the operational performance of AI systems. To address these shortcomings, this study proposes a hybrid AI-SOC architecture integrating user and entity behavior analytics, supervised machine learning (random forest), isolation forest, and large language model-based decision-support mechanisms within an Information Security Management Systems (ISMS)-aligned human-in-the-loop framework. The proposed architecture was evaluated using operational security data from the 2023 baseline and 2025 AI-SOC evaluation periods within a public university network. The comparison between evaluation periods revealed an increase in the threat detection rate from 61% to 91% (+30 percentage points), a reduction in the false-positive rate from 14% to 5% (−9 percentage points), a 69.05% reduction in mean time to detect (MTTD), and a 70.83% reduction in mean time to respond (MTTR). These findings highlight the importance of integrating algorithmic automation and adaptive AI capabilities with human expertise to improve security operations in complex institutional environments.

items.title: Detecting Small Space Objects for Space Situational Awareness with Collaborative Edge AI
items.abstract: With the rapid growth of space activities, near-Earth space is becoming increasingly congested, leading to a higher risk of spacecraft collisions and space debris generation. Recent close-proximity encounters and collision incidents necessitate efficient and cost-effective onboard systems for space object detection (SOD) and collision avoidance. While deep learning (DL) enabled Edge AI using low-cost vision sensors on single or multiple satellites has shown promises for SOD, significant challenges remain, including limited datasets, small SOD, and the lack of comprehensive performance assessments. This paper presents a collaborative Edge AI framework for multiview SOD and systematically benchmarks DL models and fusion strategies. Results show that higher image resolution significantly improves small SOD. For multiple views, image-level fusion reduces the combined communication and inference latency by 30.13% and 32.80% on average compared with feature-level and attention-based fusion across the evaluated inter-satellite link (ISL) bandwidth. For larger view sets, feature-level and attention-based fusion achieve better detection accuracy at the cost of analysis in the sensing-communication pipeline, revealing that multiview collaboration introduces minimal latency overhead under ISL constraints when reception capacity is not exceeded. Our work provides valuable design insights for future collaborative satellite network design, supporting the emerging space situational awareness and space traffic management requirements.

items.title: Diagnóstico dos riscos ocupacionais dos trabalhadores da Cooperativa de Táxis TRANSPLAYASA, Santo Domingo, 2026
items.abstract: Introduction: This research aimed to assess occupational risks among workers in the operational sector of the taxi cooperative "TRANSPLAYASA" in the Santo Domingo canton during 2026, through hazard identification, risk assessment, and the formulation of preventive measures. Materials and Methods: The study employed a mixed-methods approach with a descriptive and diagnostic scope, using a non-experimental, cross-sectional design. Data collection involved Likert-scale surveys, semi-structured interviews, direct observation forms, checklists, and the NTP 330 risk assessment matrix, applied to a sample of 140 workers. Results: The findings indicate that the primary risks present relate to ergonomic, psychosocial, mechanical, chemical, and safety factors, with exposure levels varying according to the specific job role. Discussion: Administrative roles showed a higher incidence of ergonomic and psychosocial risks, whereas the mechanic/lubrication technician and the vehicle-owning members (drivers) experienced greater exposure to mechanical, chemical, and road safety risks. Conclusions: Based on this study, a procedures manual was developed containing preventive and corrective measures aimed at controlling the identified risks. This initiative strengthens Occupational Health and Safety management, promotes the prevention of workplace accidents and occupational illnesses, and contributes to the continuous improvement of working conditions at the TRANSPLAYASA taxi cooperative.

items.title: Digital platform acceptance, perceived behavioural control, and entrepreneurship intention: The mediating role of digital entrepreneurship resilience among early-career digital entrepreneurship learners in Indonesia and China
items.abstract: This study examines the relationship between digital platform acceptance and entrepreneurial intentions among early-career digital entrepreneurship learners by integrating the Technology Acceptance Model and Theory of Planned Behaviour. Data were collected from participants across Indonesia and China, recruited through entrepreneurship training programmes and digital business communities, who had exposure to various digital entrepreneurship platforms. PLS-SEM analysis reveals that Perceived Behavioural Control emerges as the strongest predictor of Entrepreneurship Intention, closely followed by Digital Entrepreneurship Resilience. Digital Entrepreneurship Resilience partially mediates the relationships between both Perceived Ease of Use and Perceived Usefulness with Entrepreneurship Intention. The structural model explains 62.5% of the variance in entrepreneurship intention. However, the hypothesised moderating effect of Perceived Behavioural Control on the resilience-intention relationship does not reach statistical significance. These findings suggest that entrepreneurial intention development requires more than technology exposure alone, emphasising the critical roles of perceived control and adaptive capacity in digital contexts. Practical implications indicate that digital entrepreneurship training programmes should deliberately cultivate both technological resilience and behavioural control through platform-based experiential learning rather than focusing exclusively on technical skills.

items.title: Do student perceptions mirror reality? A mixed-methods study to evaluate the accuracy, utility and efficiency of AI-assisted feedback in introductory mathematics courses
items.abstract: Abstract Background Giving meaningful feedback on assignments in large introductory-level mathematics courses is a challenge. The emergence of “out of the box” Large Language Models (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini) has created a potential solution to this challenge, where the AI tool can be trained to give constructive feedback on student work. However, it is unclear whether these tools are sufficiently accurate, efficient, and trustworthy. The current study investigates the use of a bespoke AI tool to assist in giving feedback to students in two introductory mathematics courses that enroll over 400 students each and are characterized by high attrition. Results We evaluated the similarities in grades assigned by the AI tool and human graders, as well as student and grader perceptions of the feedback given by both the AI tool and human graders. We found that the tool was fairly accurate, but that perceptions of the utility of its feedback varied by condition. When evaluated as a stand-alone grading agent, the AI tool was significantly undervalued relative to human graders—both student peers and the professor. Conclusion Three themes that characterize our findings: student trust is key, the professor is irreplaceable, and graders and AI tools must be carefully trained to ensure accuracy, transparency, and trust. We conclude with a call to exercise caution in using these tools in grading assistance, particularly with respect to maintaining student trust and transparency in grading.

items.title: Effects of Explanations on Driver Situation Awareness Under Physical Adversarial Attacks in Automated Driving: A Driving Simulator Study
items.abstract: As automated driving systems (ADS) become increasingly integrated into real-world transportation, understanding how human drivers perceive and respond to system failures under adversarial conditions is critical for driving safety. Prior research has shown that human drivers overestimate ADS capabilities and lack awareness of ADS vulnerability to adversarial attacks. We conduct a laboratory study (N=32) using a driving simulator, investigating the effectiveness of explanations on enhancing human drivers' situation awareness (SA) of physical adversarial evasion attacks and their takeover performance in SAE Level 3 automated driving. We varied system reliability and attack object within subjects and explanation between subjects. Quantitative results indicated that explanations enhanced drivers' SA, without deteriorating their takeover performance. The reliability manipulation yielded non-significant results in general, probably because of explanatory content presented for the ADS detected-and-handled attacks. Nevertheless, we obtained the impact of attack object on drivers' takeover control regardless of the explanation manipulation. Qualitative results revealed that drivers often noticed abnormalities without recognizing them as attacks, while perceiving explanations as useful aids for understanding scenarios. We discuss implications of our findings and directions of future work.

items.title: Efficient Training on Multiple Consumer GPUs with RoundPipe
items.abstract: Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) on consumer-grade GPUs is highly cost-effective, yet constrained by limited GPU memory and slow PCIe interconnects. Pipeline parallelism combined with CPU offloading mitigates these hardware bottlenecks by reducing communication overhead. However, existing PP schedules suffer from an inherent limitation termed the weight binding issue. Binding uneven model stages (e.g., the LM head is large) to GPUs limits the pipeline’s throughput to that of the GPU with the heaviest load, leading to severe pipeline bubbles. In this paper, we propose RoundPipe , a novel pipeline schedule that breaks the weight binding constraint on consumer GPU servers. RoundPipe treats GPUs as a pool of stateless execution workers and dynamically dispatches computation stages across devices in a round-robin manner, achieving a near-zero-bubble pipeline. To ensure training correctness and system efficiency, RoundPipe integrates a priority-aware transfer scheduling engine, a Layerwise Model Consistency Protocol, and an automated layer partitioning algorithm. Evaluations on an 8 × RTX 4090 server demonstrate that RoundPipe achieves 1.48–2.16 × speedups over state-of-the-art baselines when fine-tuning 1.7B to 32B models. Remarkably, RoundPipe enables LoRA fine-tuning of the Qwen3-235B model with 31K sequence length on a single server. RoundPipe has been open-sourced as a Python library. items.title: Evidence for workplace accommodation and labour law policies: A focus on lived experiences of people with degenerative spine disease in Zambia
items.abstract: Degenerative Spine Disease (DSD) is a chronic condition characterised by deterioration of spinal tissues. Although DSD is associated with ageing, it has become increasingly common among younger populations. Despite its incidence, the condition's impact on work life remains under investigation in Zambia. The study aimed to explore the experiences of workplace accommodation for individuals living with DSD and to generate evidence to inform workplace accommodation and labour policies to improve support and social inclusion for individuals living with DSD in Zambia. The theoretical framework anchoring this research was a qualitative Interpretative Descriptive design and included 11 participants aged between 23 and 49 years. Participant selection was through purposeful sampling. Data were collected through face-to-face semi-structured interviews and analysed using inductive thematic analysis with NVivo software version 12. Findings: Key findings included narratives on the challenges faced and recommendations to improve work environments. Challenges included a lack of workplace understanding and accommodation; limited awareness and support in their work environment; inadequate labour laws, as participants described poor workplace policies and a disconnect between what labour laws supposedly are and the reality of their everyday workplaces; and stigma and cultural expectations, which also played a role, though more indirectly. Recommendations were: 1) clear policies and reasonable accommodations; 2) ergonomic safety; 3) hybrid work arrangements; 4) workplace awareness and Education on Chronic Health Conditions; and Regular monitoring, audits, and workplace health assessments. Conclusion: The study established the impact of DSD on individuals' work life and presented practical recommendations for employers and labour policies in Zambia. Future Research: Future research should aim to update Zambia's labour policies to reflect current work contexts and include accommodations for employees with chronic conditions.

items.title: Explainable AI for Sequential Decision-Making
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly make decisions that unfold over time: autonomous vehicles navigating traffic, robots executing manipulation sequences, game-playing agents taking moves toward their goals, and planning systems constructing multistep action sequences. Explaining such sequential behavior is fundamentally harder than explaining a single classification or regression output, yet this challenge has only recently received sustained research attention across the reinforcement learning, AI planning, robotics, and game-AI communities. This chapter provides an introduction to Explainable AI for Sequential Decision-Making (X-SDM). A unified taxonomy is developed that answers four core questions: what must be explained, who needs the explanation, how are explanations generated algorithmically, and how should they be evaluated. The taxonomy spans formal models including Markov Decision Processes and symbolic planning and covers the major families of explanation methods that have emerged across communities: contrastive and counterfactual explanations, feature importance and attribution methods, plan and goal explanations, model-reconciliation explanations, and intrinsically interpretable policies. These categories are illustrated with representative techniques, and a principled framework for user requirements grounded in situation-awareness theory is sketched. The chapter closes with ten open research questions that chart a roadmap for the field. The chapter integrates perspectives from reinforcement learning, AI planning, robotics, game AI, and cognitive science, offering students and researchers a structured entry point into this growing area.

items.title: Exploring AI Role in Enhancing or Limiting Academic Problem-Solving
items.abstract: Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and Gemini have become part of daily academic life, but little is known about how pre-service teachers use them to deal with academic problems or how teachers perceive their influence on students’ problem-solving. This qualitative, phenomenologically oriented study investigated (a) how final-semester B.Ed. students apply generative AI tools to their academic problems, and (b) how university teachers perceive the influence of AI tools on students’ problem-solving skills and what guidance they offer for productive AI use. Semi-structured interviews was conducted with twenty-three students and thirteen teachers from five public universities in Lahore, Pakistan, and the data was analyzed using thematic analysis. Two student themes were developed: patterns and purposes of AI use in academic work, and deciding between AI and independent effort. Two teacher themes were developed: teachers’ observations of AI use and its perceived influence on problem-solving, and teachers’ guidance, difficulties, and advice for productive AI use. Students reported regular use of AI for assignments, presentations, research, and lesson planning; thirteen tried problems independently first, while nine turned to AI first. All thirteen teachers observed regular and growing use of AI and agreed that it helps students understand concepts and explore approaches, but all thirteen also feared that heavy dependence could weaken critical thinking and independence. Teachers advised students to attempt tasks first, verify AI output, and write final work in their own words. Because the findings rest on participants’ reported views, they describe perceptions and not measured effects on problem-solving ability.

items.title: Exploring diminishing returns for multimodal dynamic event expression in mixed reality
items.abstract: Expressing dynamic events in Mixed Reality (MR) requires users to communicate continuous spatiotemporal information, including entity trajectories, interactions, and temporal dynamics. This task is fundamentally constrained by the linearization bottleneck: human mental models preserve rich relational structures holistically, yet conventional output channels, such as speech, force them to be serialized into sequential streams. Multimodal interaction offers a promising solution by distributing information across complementary channels, but it remains unclear how different multimodal strategies perform as spatiotemporal complexity increases. This paper addresses these two knowledge gaps: the lack of a systematic analysis of decomposing dynamic events and the absence of empirical evidence comparing multimodal expression strategies under controlled-complexity conditions. We propose a structured analysis that decomposes dynamic events into fundamental information blocks and establishes a complexity taxonomy. Building on this analysis, we design sequential and parallel multimodal expression strategies and evaluate them alongside sequential (unimodal) speech as complete interaction strategies in a controlled user study using abstract geometric micro-worlds. Under error-free speech–gaze fusion provided through a Wizard-of-Oz setup, parallel multimodal input maintains a substantial completion-time advantage across the tested event levels. However, its subjective benefits decrease as coordination demands rise. When events include asynchronous timing or causal interactions, parallel input is no longer rated significantly higher than sequential multimodal input, though this does not imply equivalence. These findings suggest a boundary condition for the subjective benefits of the parallel strategy, providing design implications for adaptive multimodal MR systems.

items.title: False data injection detection in nuclear power plants using autoencoder with latent-conditioned Mahalanobis scoring
items.abstract: As instrumentation and control (I&C) systems in nuclear power plants (NPPs) are digitalized, cybersecurity concerns have grown. A particular concern is false data injection (FDI) attacks, which can induce malfunctions of plant systems and degrade the situational awareness of main control room operators. Against such attacks, monitoring the integrity of process data can serve as a defensive barrier, and autoencoders have been studied as a promising tool for this purpose. However, their reconstruction error varies across operating conditions even for normal data, which forces the detection threshold above the errors of rare but normal conditions and allows well-crafted manipulations to evade detection. To improve sensitivity where false alarms must be minimized, this study proposes latent-conditioned Mahalanobis scoring, which requires no modification of the conventional autoencoder. The method clusters the latent vectors of calibration data, estimates the mean and covariance of reconstruction residuals per cluster, and scores a query input by the Mahalanobis distance under its nearest clusters' statistics. Experiments with emergency operation data from an NPP simulator and 10 synthetic FDI scenarios injected during accident conditions show that the proposed score outperforms the conventional reconstruction-error score and other scoring methods at high specificity levels.

items.title: FlexMARL: Graph-Driven Rollout-Training Co-Design for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Despite algorithm-level innovations for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), the underlying infrastructure for large-scale MARL remains underexplored. Existing training frameworks primarily optimize for single-agent scenarios and fail to capture the graph-structured nature of MARL. This fundamental mismatch leads to three MARL-specific challenges: topology-induced rollout skew, critical path synchronization barriers, and dynamic training demand. To bridge this gap, we propose FlexMARL, a graph-driven rollout-training co-designed framework for large-scale LLM-based MARL. FlexMARL introduces the multi-agent execution graph (MEG) and materializes the intermediate representation as the MEG Store, which provides decentralized multi-table storage and serves as the data hub for system components. Built around the MEG Store, the Rollout Engine develops dependency parallel sampling with hierarchical load balancing, which reduces inference latency and balances intra-agent/inter-agent loads. The Joint Orchestrator exploits an agent-level asynchronous pipeline to mitigate the critical path synchronization barriers while maintaining consistency. The Training Engine achieves on-demand resource allocation by collectively managing training processes for individual agents. The training states of different agents are swapped via location-agnostic communication APIs. Empirical results on a production cluster demonstrate that FlexMARL achieves up to 7.3 × speedup and improves hardware utilization by up to 5.6 × compared to existing frameworks.

items.title: From Objective Compromise to Structure-Enabled Intelligence: Reshaping the Scientific Paradigm of AI
items.abstract: Mainstream artificial intelligence systems, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), are fundamentally constructed upon the Optimization-Driven (OD) paradigm. This paradigm can be characterized as an ill-posed optimization problem within a high-dimensional parameter space. When confronted with real-world scenarios characterized by noise and conflicting constraints, the logic of global error minimization inherently induces a strong smoothing effect. Consequently, this yields statistical compromise solutions that flatten local features, making it arduous to overcome the inherent bottleneck of Out-of-Distribution (OOD) generalization. Existing AI models generate outputs purely based on statistical probabilities. They lack the capacity to autonomously discern truth from falsehood or establish causal logic, thereby lacking genuine cognitive intelligence. To address the ontological limitations of the OD paradigm, this paper proposes a novel paradigm termed \textit{Structure-Enabled Intelligence}. This approach abandons the conventional path of relying solely on computing power scaling and data fitting to achieve emergent intelligence. Instead, it embeds mathematical structures and physical mechanisms as underlying priors into the algorithmic architecture, constraining the model's solving process with structured scientific rules. Through this paradigm shift from ``data-driven objective fitting'' to ``mechanism-structure dominance,'' the proposed approach fundamentally mitigates the issue of statistical compromise, enhances the model's extrapolation and generalization capabilities, and simultaneously reshapes human-AI synergy by upholding human subjectivity in scientific cognition.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: Fundamental Limits of Statistical Watermarking for LLMs with Fixed and Optimizable Common Randomness
items.abstract: Watermarking has emerged as an important technique for distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written text. However, most existing work is primarily empirical, relies on ad hoc watermarking designs, and lacks a fundamental understanding of the performance limits. In this paper, we propose a unified theoretical framework for statistical watermarking of large language models (LLMs), casting the problem as an independence test between generated text and common randomness and jointly designing the watermarking embedder and the detector. Our objective is to maximize detection power while controlling the worst-case false positive rate (FPR) and limiting distortion to text quality. A central focus of our framework is the design of the common randomness, which plays a critical role in both watermark embedding and detection. We characterize the fundamental limits of statistical watermarking under both fixed and optimizable common randomness. Our results show that optimizing the common randomness does not improve the fundamental limits: the best achievable performance is the same as that with fixed common randomness. Nevertheless, common randomness design remains highly important because it can substantially simplify detector design. In particular, with optimizable common randomness, a fixed, deterministic, and model-agnostic detector can achieve optimal performance. We further study a practical setting with fixed uniform common randomness and a fixed deterministic detector, and characterize its performance gap relative to the optimizable case, thereby demonstrating the practical value of optimizable common randomness.

items.title: Generation of protein conformations using a simple inverted transformer
items.abstract: Molecular dynamics is an extremely powerful approach for studying protein behavior, but it requires enormous computational resources to obtain an adequate sampling of possible conformations. Recently, thanks to successes in predicting three-dimensional protein structures, there has been an explosion of research exploring the opportunities offered by deep learning to address the problem of protein conformational landscape. In this work, an artificial intelligence system based on a variant of the Transformer architecture is introduced and applied to the problem of determining the ensemble of three-dimensional structures that a protein can access and their statistical weight. After being trained on a dataset of conformations of a particular protein obtained using classical all-atom molecular dynamics, this neural network is able to directly generate physically plausible protein conformations similar to those obtained both through molecular dynamics and experimentally. The ordered sequence of conformations obtained as output of the neural network rapidly converges towards the most populated regions of the protein's conformational landscape, suggesting that the system may have learned not only the protein's three-dimensional organization but also the thermodynamic weights of the various feasible conformations. These features, combined with its simplicity and low computational load, make this Transformer variant an ideal candidate for the development of systems capable of performing generative molecular dynamics.

items.title: Generative AI dependence, perceived AI threat, career adaptability, and post-graduation anxiety among Chinese university students: a cross-sectional survey
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has become part of university students’ everyday learning, yet research on its consequences has focused mainly on immediate learning outcomes. This study examined whether the way students use generative AI in their studies is connected with how they appraise their professional futures. Drawing on research on cognitive offloading, appraisal theories of stress and emotion, and career construction theory, I tested whether AI dependence—letting AI do the cognitive work of learning tasks and accepting its output with little verification—rather than frequency of use was associated with anxiety about post-graduation destinations, whether perceived AI threat accounted for part of this association, and whether career adaptability buffered the threat–anxiety link. In a cross-sectional survey of 965 Chinese university students, AI dependence was positively associated with post-graduation anxiety when frequency was controlled (β = .36), whereas frequency was not (β = .00). Perceived AI threat accounted for an indirect association amounting to 41% of the total. Career adaptability was associated with lower anxiety, but, contrary to the buffering hypothesis, the threat–anxiety association was stronger among more adaptable students, and adaptability was unrelated to anxiety when perceived threat was high. In exploratory analyses, critical use of AI output was associated with higher adaptability but not with threat or anxiety. Because the data are cross-sectional and self-reported, the findings are associations compatible with the proposed pathway rather than evidence of causation. Implications for AI-integrated teaching and assessment, AI literacy, and career guidance in higher education are discussed.

items.title: GenOR‐Twin: a semantic middleware for integrating operational discourse with mathematical optimization
items.abstract: Abstract We introduce GenOR‐Twin, a neuro‐symbolic framework that bridges the translation gap between unstructured operational logs and rigorous mathematical optimization. Our architecture uniquely positions large language models as semantic translators rather than direct solvers, ensuring that the system retains the feasibility guarantees of exact combinatorial methods. We design a dynamic constraint injection mechanism (the runtime translation of qualitative disruption events into formal mathematical constraints) that allows the system to structurally modify the optimization problem's feasibility region in real time based on qualitative human inputs. The resulting bidirectional coupling—where operational observations update the virtual model state and optimized decisions are reflected back into the knowledge graph—satisfies the synchronization requirement of a proper digital twin. The framework features an adaptive decision policy that automatically selects between low‐complexity schedule repair and full re‐optimization by analyzing the available system slack. Finally, we demonstrate the generalization of this approach across six distinct optimization domains, showing that static models can adapt to real‐world operational uncertainty.

items.title: Ghost Approvals: Approval-Provenance Failure in Agentic AI Frameworks
items.abstract: Agentic AI systems increasingly execute actions for users, including transfers, deployments, account changes, and data release. Human approval gates are meant to prevent these actions from running until a reviewer has inspected the proposed action and issued a decision. Because approval can arrive after a delay, frameworks often persist workflow state and resume later. The resume path therefore becomes a security boundary: it must distinguish evidence that a human approved from approval-shaped values stored in mutable state. We define Approval-Provenance Failure as a condition in which a workflow resume path treats mutable approval-relevant state as evidence that a trusted human approval path produced a decision. Our adversary can write approval-relevant workflow state, but cannot use the approval path, change the model, modify tool code, invoke the tool directly, write the business database, mint a valid approval artifact, or access the approval issuer key. We evaluate 18 agent frameworks with human approval, interruption, or pause-resume behavior. Thirteen are exposed, three are resistant, and two are non-applicable. In exposed cases, state-only approval forgery causes gated action execution after a negative control blocks ordinary resume. The failure also forges the evidence of human oversight itself: across 500 paired audit traces, genuine and forged records are statistically indistinguishable, with exact-match rate 1.0 and AUC 0.5 under the tested native audit-field projection, while provenance evidence separates them with AUC 1.0. Finally, we evaluate a provenance-bound approval artifact that authenticates the decision with a MAC or digital signature and is verified at resume time. The full artifact check blocks 13 adversarial variants on five representative targets with microsecond-scale verification cost.

items.title: Giving Operators a Voice Without Giving up Safety: A Safety-Gated Sociotechnical Architecture for Natural-Language Preferences in Human–Robot Collaborative Cells
items.abstract: Operators of collaborative cells have no runtime channel to ask the robot to slow down, leave fragile parts to them or serve them first. Language models can interpret such requests, but their failure modes cannot be listed in advance. This paper separates interpretation from authority: a local model renders each request as a candidate in a small typed language; a deterministic gate admits only candidates that are well formed, raised at the speaker’s own terminal, confined to their zones and tightening; and speed-and-separation monitoring runs below the scheduler, beyond any request. The problem is formalised, and a hazard analysis locates the main residual risk in mode confusion. In a simulated two-operator cell with a Doosan M1013, costs bore little relation to how modest a request sounded: routing fragile parts to an operator cost 1.3% of throughput but raised protective stops sevenfold, and a speed cap cost 6.4%, with almost half of it being borne by the colleague. Six local open-weight models responded within 1.2 s on one GPU and rendered 41–81% of requests exactly. No candidate outside the speaker’s authority or the plant’s limits was admitted, and under the recommended speed law, a full-arm oracle found no breach of the protective distance.

items.title: gKSM: GPU Memory Deduplication at Driver Layer for Serverless LLM Inference
items.abstract: In serverless LLM inference, cloud providers commonly locate multiple instances on a single GPU to improve utilization. However, each instance independently maintains its model weights and runtime state, making duplicate GPU memory the primary bottleneck. Memory deduplication is a widely-used technique for eliminating duplicate data in CPU systems, but extending it to GPU memory faces fundamental challenges. Effective GPU memory deduplication must avoid redundant data movement between CPU and GPU while preserving write isolation for shared pages without native copy-on-write (COW) support. This paper presents gKSM, a transparent GPU memory deduplication framework for serverless LLM inference. gKSM addresses these challenges through CPU-GPU collaborative hash management that offloads hash computation to GPU kernels, zero-copy model weight deduplication that eliminates duplication before model weight transfer, and a cross-privilege page fault handler that combines a lightweight kernel hook and CUDA Virtual Memory Management (VMM) remapping in the user space. gKSM also designs a stable page scanning algorithm and a reuse-aware placement policy in cluster scale. Experiments show that gKSM reduces GPU memory usage by 59.8% while maintaining high throughput compared to ServerlessLLM. Under memory constrained workloads, gKSM improves aggregate throughput by 2.15 × and supports five instances concurrently. In cluster level simulation, gKSM achieves a service rate of 99.97%, compared to 78.2% for SLInfer and 26.9% for ServerlessLLM.

items.title: HyperDBDiag: Multi-Root-Cause Identification and Operator-Level Localization for Database Performance Anomalies
items.abstract: Database performance anomalies in modern production environments are not always triggered by a single cause. Instead, they often arise from the concurrent interaction of multiple causes within the same time window, posing substantial challenges to accurate operator-level root-cause analysis. When multiple root causes interact through shared resources, metric anomalies may be amplified, attenuated, or masked. Consequently, salient local anomalies may no longer correspond directly to the actual root causes, making conventional single-path diagnosis and shallow correlation-based methods prone to misdiagnosis. To address this challenge, we propose HyperDBDiag, a method for multi-root-cause identification and operator-level localization of database performance anomalies. HyperDBDiag connects root causes, performance metrics, SQL templates, and execution operators in a knowledge graph, captures joint anomaly patterns across metrics with a metric hypergraph, and uses a constrained LLM to determine the final root-cause set and provide remediation suggestions. When finer-grained localization is possible, HyperDBDiag also identifies the associated anomalous SQL statements and execution operators. We evaluate HyperDBDiag on a database performance anomaly dataset constructed using DB-MAGS. Experimental results show that HyperDBDiag effectively reduces graph complexity while improving root-cause localization accuracy.

items.title: HYPIC: Position-Independent Caching for Hybrid-Attention LLM Serving
items.abstract: In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agentic LLM serving, prompts are assembled from multiple independent segments into long contexts, making prefill dominate the computation cost. To reduce this cost, position-independent caching (PIC) admits KV reuse for non-contiguous segments across requests, while hybrid-attention models reduce computational complexity using linear attention. However, existing PIC methods break down on hybrid-attention models because their per-token KV-cache reuse primitives do not transfer to per-request recurrent states. In this work, we present Hypic , the first system to accelerate hybrid-attention LLM serving with position-independent caching. For linear-attention layers, we identify the segment-cumulative transition operator as the missing algebraic primitive and cache it for each segment, enabling near-exact and constant-time state composition. For the remaining full-attention layers, we construct a small seam window to propagate hidden states through the linear-attention layers, so that cross-segment attention can be repaired by recomputation. Finally, Hypic introduces segment parallelism, which parallelizes cache-miss prefill across instances, turning long cold requests into an accelerable workload. Evaluated across four hybrid-attention models and five workloads, Hypic reduces time-to-first-token (TTFT) by 3.25 × on average and improves QPS by 1.66 × over Prefix Cache, while preserving task quality with a 1.71-point gap from Full Recompute.

items.title: Instructor-designed AI improves learning in a randomized trial across 19 universities
items.abstract: Universities are alarmed by recent evidence that artificial intelligence (AI) can undermine learning, with students prescribed generic chatbots or centrally designed AI tools performing worse. In a pre-registered randomized controlled trial across 7,200 students at 19 universities over three semesters, we tested whether AI designed by frontline instructors can improve learning. We encouraged instructors to design AI solutions they believed would best help their students. Drawing on their unique knowledge of their classes and students, the instructors created a wide array of innovations. We show that these instructor-designed AI innovations improved student learning, measured by AI-proof assessments (proctored, in-person examinations). We found no change in student engagement, measured by course activity records, or satisfaction, measured by course evaluations. Our findings demonstrate that AI can improve student learning when its adoption is frontline-driven, with instructors empowered to design and refine AI solutions for their own classrooms.

items.title: KECEMASAN BERBAHASA JERMAN DALAM PROSES PEMBELAJARAN PADA MAHASISWA PENDIDIKAN BAHASA JERMAN UNIVERSITAS NEGERI MALANG
items.abstract: This study was motivated by the presence of anxiety in the process of learning and using German among university students, particularly when facing communication, evaluation, and judgment from others. This study aimed to describe German language anxiety among students of the German Language Education Study Program at Universitas Negeri Malang. A quantitative approach with a descriptive method was employed involving 63 students. Data were collected using a 28-item instrument covering three aspects: communication apprehension, test anxiety, and fear of negative evaluation. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics through response distribution and score categorization. The results showed that 66.7% of students were categorized as having high anxiety, 25.4% as moderate, and 7.9% as low. Among the three aspects, test anxiety was the most prominent, with 68.3% of students classified in the high category, followed by fear of negative evaluation at 65.1% and communication apprehension at 61.9%. These findings indicate that German language anxiety among the students was generally high, particularly in situations involving the evaluation of German language proficiency. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh adanya kecemasan yang dapat muncul dalam proses pembelajaran dan penggunaan bahasa Jerman pada mahasiswa, terutama ketika menghadapi situasi komunikasi, evaluasi kemampuan, dan penilaian dari orang lain. Kondisi tersebut penting diperhatikan karena penggunaan bahasa Jerman merupakan bagian utama dalam proses pembelajaran mahasiswa Program Studi Pendidikan Bahasa Jerman. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui gambaran kecemasan berbahasa Jerman pada mahasiswa Program Studi Pendidikan Bahasa Jerman Universitas Negeri Malang. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode deskriptif. Responden penelitian berjumlah 63 mahasiswa dan data dikumpulkan menggunakan instrumen kecemasan berbahasa Jerman yang terdiri atas 28 butir pernyataan dengan tiga aspek, yaitu communication apprehension, test anxiety, dan fear of negative evaluation. Data dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif melalui distribusi jawaban dan kategorisasi skor. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa 42 mahasiswa (66,7%) berada pada kategori kecemasan tinggi, 16 mahasiswa (25,4%) berada pada kategori sedang, dan 5 mahasiswa (7,9%) berada pada kategori rendah. Berdasarkan aspek, test anxiety memiliki proporsi kategori tinggi paling besar, yaitu 68,3%, diikuti fear of negative evaluation sebesar 65,1% dan communication apprehension sebesar 61,9%. Dengan demikian, kecemasan berbahasa Jerman pada mahasiswa dalam penelitian ini tergolong tinggi, dengan kecemasan terhadap evaluasi kemampuan bahasa Jerman sebagai aspek yang paling menonjol.

items.title: Keep on Keeping On, With a Machine: Artificial Intelligence and the Calibration of Entrepreneurial Persistence
items.abstract: Entrepreneurs increasingly turn to artificial intelligence (AI) when deciding whether to continue a struggling venture, yet persistence theory locates the antecedents of persistence either within the entrepreneur or within human social networks. We theorize AI as a distinct, non-human antecedent of entrepreneurial persistence. Building on the psychological resource approach to persistence, escalation and threshold theories, and the AI Entrepreneurial Agency Framework, we distinguish two pathways. Through a resource pathway, AI supplies psychological resources that raise persistence intensity and loosen its dependence on the entrepreneur's internal resources. Through an epistemic pathway, AI shapes the feedback on which persistence decisions rest and thereby governs persistence calibration, which we define as the responsiveness of persistence to diagnostic disconfirming evidence. Five propositions specify when the pathways combine into AI-amplified escalation, how the Knightian uncertainty of the decision widens a gap between confidence and calibration, and how agentic AI attenuates the decision points at which founders confront adversity. A temporal extension explains how sustained AI scaffolding can render persistence fragile. The framework reconciles optimistic and pessimistic accounts of AI in entrepreneurship and offers testable implications for small business owners, advisors, and AI designers.

items.title: Kepengikutan (Followership) dan Perilaku Proaktif Karyawan: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis
items.abstract: Menurunnya keterlibatan karyawan secara global berpotensi melemahkan inisiatif di tempat kerja, sementara bukti tentang kepengikutan dan perilaku proaktif karyawan tersebar pada beragam konstruk, konteks, dan metode. Penelitian ini bertujuan memetakan karakteristik, pola hubungan, mekanisme, dan kesenjangan penelitian tentang kedua topik tersebut pada periode 2016–2026. Penelitian ini menggunakan tinjauan literatur sistematis yang mengikuti pedoman Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. Data sekunder berupa artikel jurnal empiris dikumpulkan dari basis data Scopus dan SAGE Journals. Kualitas studi dinilai dengan Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool 2018, dan data dianalisis dengan statistik deskriptif serta sintesis naratif. Sebanyak 21 studi empiris memenuhi kriteria inklusi, dengan 12 studi terbit pada periode 2024–2026. Bukti terkonsentrasi di Asia Timur dan Eropa, dengan Tiongkok menyumbang studi terbanyak (7 studi), didominasi desain kuantitatif (18 studi), dan belum mencakup Indonesia. Hanya 10 studi yang menjadikan kepengikutan sebagai konstruk utama, sedangkan studi lainnya memakai istilah pengikut sebagai sebutan bawahan. Hubungan Followership dan perilaku proaktif terpetakan dalam empat jalur, yaitu anteseden kepemimpinan dan konteks, kepengikutan sebagai prediktor, respons pemimpin terhadap perilaku proaktif, dan batas konseptual kepengikutan. Penelitian ini mengusulkan model timbal balik yang menempatkan orientasi peran kepengikutan sebagai mekanisme penghubung. Penelitian selanjutnya perlu mengukur kepengikutan secara eksplisit, memakai desain longitudinal multisumber, dan menguji konteks Indonesia.

items.title: LABOR RELATIONS IN AGRIBUSINESS PRESENT CHALLENGES CONCERNING LEGAL PROTECTION, ECONOMIC INEQUALITIES, AND OCCUPATIONAL CONDITIONS
items.abstract: Labor relations in agribusiness present challenges concerning legal protection, economic inequalities, and occupational conditions. In the state of Amazonas, the diversity of agricultural, extractive, and riverine activities adds specific nuances to this analysis. This study examines how scientific literature addresses the rights and obligations within agribusiness labor relations, identifies factors associated with labor conflicts, and explores potential preventive measures tailored to the reality of the Amazon region. The objective was to analyze these relations, identify vulnerability factors, and systematize dimensions for conflict prevention. A qualitative, exploratory, and descriptive narrative literature review was conducted, involving a thematic analysis of 12 articles published between 2014 and 2025. The findings highlight issues related to wage inequality, precarious working conditions, occupational risks, power imbalances in negotiations, and the violation of rights. The analysis also underscores the necessity of distinguishing between formal employment, self-employment, and family-based production. As a contribution, five preventive dimensions were systematized: legal and contractual protection; occupational health and safety; corporate responsibility; equity and social protection; and socio-territorial suitability. It is concluded that conflict prevention requires an integrated approach that considers legal obligations, production conditions, and social vulnerabilities. The effectiveness of the proposed dimensions remains subject to empirical evaluation.

items.title: Large language model agent simulations of individual differences in social interactions
items.abstract: A key challenge in the behavioral sciences is the lack of formal models that capture individual differences in social interactions. At the same time, recent advances in artificial intelligence offer new opportunities to simulate and assess interpersonal behavior at scale. In this study, we introduce an agent-based modeling framework that uses large language models (LLMs) to simulate short-term social interactions. Within a dyadic interaction cycle, an LLM-based agent continually adjusts its interpersonal behavior (agency and communion) to its prior behavior, the partner’s behavior, and the combined influence of behavioral defaults (differences in default behavioral tendencies) and interpersonal reactivities (differences in reactions to partner behaviors). We derive a mathematical model that formalizes how interpersonal behavior unfolds across the interaction, evaluate the model in simulations, illustrate how the framework expresses these interpersonal dynamics in natural language, and outline the framework’s flexibility for simulating individual differences in practical applications across the behavioral sciences.

items.title: Large language model agent simulations of individual differences in social interactions
items.abstract: A key challenge in the behavioral sciences is the lack of formal models that capture individual differences in social interactions. At the same time, recent advances in artificial intelligence offer new opportunities to simulate and assess interpersonal behavior at scale. In this study, we introduce an agent-based modeling framework that uses large language models (LLMs) to simulate short-term social interactions. Within a dyadic interaction cycle, an LLM-based agent continually adjusts its interpersonal behavior (agency and communion) to its prior behavior, the partner’s behavior, and the combined influence of behavioral defaults (differences in default behavioral tendencies) and interpersonal reactivities (differences in reactions to partner behaviors). We derive a mathematical model that formalizes how interpersonal behavior unfolds across the interaction, evaluate the model in simulations, illustrate how the framework expresses these interpersonal dynamics in natural language, and outline the framework’s flexibility for simulating individual differences in practical applications across the behavioral sciences.

items.title: Large Language Models for AI Infrastructure
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to design, optimize, and operate the infrastructure behind AI training and serving, yet the literature remains fragmented across hardware design, machine learning systems, electronic design automation, and high-performance computing. We present a comprehensive survey of LLM-assisted AI infrastructure across its lifecycle, from accelerator design and kernel engineering to compilation, deployment, operations, data management, and energy optimization. We organize the literature by the primary resource the LLM manages: artifact-centric methods for computational artifacts, operational-centric methods for deployment context and system state, and resource-centric methods for data and energy. These categories span the lifecycle and cover AI-specific concerns such as distributed-training configuration, inference serving, GPU-cluster scheduling, and data loading. Building on this taxonomy, we conduct a cross-study quantitative synthesis of reported results. Because studies adopt heterogeneous benchmarks, baselines, hardware, and metrics, we compare methods only where evaluation conditions permit and align results along common dimensions: functional correctness, execution performance, throughput, resource and energy consumption, operational outcomes, and optimization cost, keeping each result's native metric, baseline, and setting rather than collapsing them into a single score. This comparison reveals where LLM-driven methods yield consistent gains, how reported gains in workload orchestration depend on the evaluation environment, from simulators to real clusters and production, and where evidence is still lacking. Together, the taxonomy, lifecycle perspective, and quantitative evaluation provide an evidence-grounded reference for LLM-driven engineering of AI infrastructure.

items.title: Learning from Mutants: Teaching Small Language Models to Synthesise Loop Invariants
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have proven promising for synthesising loop invariants, a long-standing obstacle to automated program verification. Yet, frontier LLMs are typically accessible only through third-party APIs, hampering reproducibility and local deployment. Small language models (SLMs) sidestep these obstacles but require task-specific fine-tuning, for which high-quality training data is needed. We present a failure-driven data curation method for fine-tuning language models to synthesise loop invariants. Inspired by mutation testing, our approach applies semantic mutation operators to ground-truth invariants, producing semantic mutants that induce verification failure. Each mutant is paired with verifier feedback and its ground-truth counterpart, yielding training examples for feedback-guided invariant refinement. Whereas the vast space of mutants is a long-standing burden in mutation testing, it becomes an asset when generating training data, multiplying the examples obtainable from a fixed set of verified programs. We implement our approach for Dafny, augmenting an existing synthetic dataset of verified programs, and introduce a framework that iteratively refines candidate invariants using verifier feedback. On 472 DafnyBench programs, our best-performing fine-tuned Gemma-4-E4B configuration verifies 50.8% of programs zero-shot, compared to 8.1% for the base model, a 6.3$\times$ improvement. Higher-order mutants prove more effective as training data than first-order mutants, and adding mutation-based examples to direct synthesis examples, in which invariants are removed rather than mutated, improves performance under iterative refinement. Our approach also transfers to Qwen3.5-4B, whose zero-shot verification rate rises from 9.3% to 53.6%.

items.title: Leveraging open-weight language models for automated patient record linkage
items.abstract: Patient record linkage is essential for integrating healthcare data fragmented across institutions and systems into unified, longitudinal health profiles that support disease surveillance, research, and policy-making. This study evaluates open-weight language models, including large language models (LLMs), for automating the two key steps of patient record linkage, blocking and matching, against conventional probabilistic linkage. Using real-world data from the Missouri Cancer Registry and Research Center, we linked patient records from a consolidated cancer registry and an electronic pathology reporting system. Probabilistic linkage using the Fellegi–Sunter model served as the baseline. For blocking, we fine-tuned a RoBERTa-based embedding model to retrieve similar records and compared it with a hybrid rule-based and probabilistic approach. For matching, we evaluated RoBERTa and open-weight generative LLMs from the Llama, Mistral, Gemma, and DeepSeek families (3 to 70 billion parameters) under fine-tuned and zero-shot settings. Performance on 52,119 test record pairs was assessed against manually reviewed labels using precision, recall, F1 score, and error counts, with bootstrap confidence intervals and McNemar’s exact tests. Embedding-based blocking reduced candidate pairs by 92% with 99.87% recall, whereas hybrid blocking achieved a 95% reduction with 100% recall. All fine-tuned generative LLMs made fewer errors than the probabilistic baseline (6 to 11 versus 17), although these differences were not statistically significant. Their errors largely differed from the baseline’s; referring only their disagreements to human review would require reviewing fewer than 1% of ambiguous pairs. Zero-shot performance varied widely: Gemma-3-27B showed no statistically significant difference from the baseline, whereas two of the smallest models failed. The reasoning model DeepSeek-R1-70B made more errors and was substantially slower than its non-reasoning counterpart. Fine-tuned open-weight LLMs had numerically fewer errors than the probabilistic linkage baseline, but this was not statistically significant, with complementary error patterns; fine-tuning, rather than model size, made their performance consistent. These models can be deployed locally without transmitting protected health information, making them well suited to support classification of ambiguous record pairs, reduce manual review, and improve completeness of patient-level data for cancer surveillance and research. Hybrid blocking remained preferable to embedding-based blocking for structured patient records.

items.title: Linking Organisational Learning and Work Engagement: A Narrative Review of Theoretical Mechanisms and Organisational Outcomes
items.abstract: Organisational learning (OL) and work engagement (WE) are related but conceptually distinct constructs. This critical narrative review examines empirical associations between learning-organisation characteristics and engagement, while distinguishing organisational learning capability from employee training and perceived development opportunities. Searches of Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO and Google Scholar were undertaken between December 2025 and September 2026; English-language sources were selected by J.M.A.F. and V.G. The synthesis distinguishes direct observational evidence, adjacent research and theoretical mechanisms. Studies from information technology, banking and other sectors generally report positive but dimension-specific associations, and statistical mediation models have linked learning culture, WE and innovative behaviour. More recent findings suggest that employee characteristics may moderate these associations. However, measurement heterogeneity, possible confounding and predominantly cross-sectional designs preclude robust causal or reciprocal inferences. The Job Demands–Resources (JD–R) model proposes an instrumental resource pathway; Social Exchange Theory proposes a complementary perceived-investment and reciprocity pathway. Healthcare is discussed as an applied context, not as the exclusive evidence base: clinical hierarchies, interprofessional coordination, staffing pressures, emotional labour and shift work may change the operation of these pathways. The review identifies priorities for temporally ordered, multilevel and intervention studies, and provides conditional rather than causal practice implications.

items.title: LLM Facilitation of Group Decision-Making
items.abstract: Human groups often fail to integrate information distributed across their members, converging on incorrect decisions. We ask whether large language models (LLMs) can help groups reach the correct decision in such settings. In an online, chat-based experiment, 138 three-person groups (N = 414) completed a hidden-profile hiring task that required selecting the best candidate using public information available to all group members and private information available only to individual members. The randomized human-subject experiment included three conditions: no facilitation, an individual-level LLM that messaged each member privately, and a group-level LLM that messaged the whole group. The LLM facilitation consisted of adaptive interventions that summarized the discussion, nudged quiet members, and played devil's advocate. The LLM did not know which candidate was correct. Both LLM conditions significantly increased the rate at which groups reached consensus on the correct candidate, from 32.6% without facilitation to 56.5% with LLM facilitation. LLM-facilitated groups exchanged more consensus messages signaling agreement on the group's choice. Participants in the group-level condition also disclosed significantly more information about the correct candidate, whereas those receiving individual-level facilitation repeated public information less often. Finally, group-level facilitation received more favorable usability ratings than individual-level facilitation. These results show that LLMs can deliver adaptive, theory-informed interventions that improve group decision-making, and that the design of these interventions may shape how people respond to them.

items.title: LLM Trading Agents Earn Beta, Not Alpha: A Look-Ahead-Free Benchmark
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) trading agents now trade stocks for their users, and benchmarks rank models by their agents' returns. Yet a single run's return says little about skill. In our study, two runs of the same model that differed only in the random seed ended 5.2 points apart on average, so telling skill from luck takes many backtests across markets, models and seeds. However, live arenas trade each day only once, and backtests either use the few months after a model's training cutoff or run on years the model may remember, often with news joined to prices by calendar date. In this paper, we present rta-bench-1, a backtest over three US markets (a rally, a bear market and a crash). It shows each headline only after its publication minute, plays each period blind and named, and checks every run for look-ahead. It also splits each return into factor exposure and alpha and scores every decision against random choices of the same day and sector. In 91 runs of six models from four vendors, no alpha was significant, market and style exposure accounted for a median 78% of the return, and the decisions did no better than random stocks of the same sector. The agents bought the stocks with the most positive news, yet in ablations they earned as much without their headlines. Still, the agents carried out rules reliably, since a single cash rule in the prompt cut a GPT-based agent's share in stocks by 30.3 points in all six pairs. Builders should therefore supply the edge themselves and report exposures and alpha, and benchmarks should replay news by publication time.

items.title: Long-Horizon Forecasting of Complete Financial Statements with Forma
items.abstract: Specialist training beats generalist scale when forecasting financial statements. To our knowledge, no prior work jointly forecasts complete financial statements beyond one year, yet in a discounted-cash-flow valuation most firm value sits past that window. We release ProForma-20Q, a reproducible benchmark for forecasting 78 statement line items 1–20 quarters ahead, for anonymized firms, from past statements and an industry code, scored by change-space R2. On it, Forma, a transformer that reads statements as sets of (account, quarter, value) tuples and maximizes a masked-tuple Gaussian likelihood, beats every competitor we field: classical machine learning, chained gradient boosting, a zero-shot time-series foundation model, and frontier large language models. Its lead widens with horizon, where valuation needs accuracy most, and its Gaussian predictive intervals never under-cover. Forma’s forecasts nearly satisfy accounting identities; exact coherence is recoverable at a small accuracy cost. Its tuple interface supports scenario analysis without retraining, and we show that pinning future revenue paths sharpens the rest of the statement.

items.title: Low-Latency LLM-Based Streaming Multi-Talker ASR with Verifiable Rewards
items.abstract: LLM-based architectures offer strong generalization and instruction-following capabilities for streaming automatic speech recognition (ASR), but multi-talker use introduces coupled transcription, attribution, and latency challenges. Our wearable setting requires real-time transcription of a conversation between a near-field device wearer and a far-field partner. Because partial hypotheses are rendered on persistent sides of a dialogue UI, speaker roles cannot be permuted and each speaker tag must precede its turn. These sparse tags are weakly optimized by supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while committing to a leading tag can delay the text that follows. We therefore post-train a streaming LLM-based ASR model with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), combining a fixed-role Speaker-Attributed WER (SA-WER) grader with a turn-level onset-delay reward. On an eight-direction multi-talker cohort, SA-WER RL reduces SA-WER from $20.51\%$ for SFT to $13.14\%$. Adding the delay objective reduces onset $p50$ by $65\%$ (from $0.918\,\text{s}$ to $0.320\,\text{s}$) and $p90$ by $44\%$ (from $1.389\,\text{s}$ to $0.780\,\text{s}$) relative to SA-WER-only RL, while achieving $12.70\%$ SA-WER. These results demonstrate that fixed-role recognition quality and streaming responsiveness can be improved jointly.

items.title: MENTAL HEALTH AND OCCUPATIONAL DISORDERS AMONG NURSING PROFESSIONALS IN THE STATE OF SANTA CATARINA, BRAZIL
items.abstract: Work-related mental disorders have become one of the leading causes of occupational leave among healthcare professionals, particularly in nursing, due to work overload, long working hours, institutional pressure, and constant exposure to situations of suffering. Considering this scenario, this study aimed to analyze the epidemiological profile of leaves of absence due to mental and behavioral disorders among nursing professionals in the state of Santa Catarina, Brazil, from 2020 to 2024. To this end, a quantitative, descriptive, and epidemiological study was conducted using secondary data from the National Observatory of Occupational Health and Safety (SmartLab), regarding absences classified under ICD-10 codes F00–F99, analyzed through descriptive statistics. The findings revealed variations in the number of absences throughout the study period, with an initial reduction followed by a significant increase in the final years of the historical series. Depressive disorders, anxiety disorders, and stress-related and adjustment disorders were the most prevalent diagnoses. Nursing technicians represented the professional category with the highest number of absences, followed by nursing assistants and registered nurses. It is concluded that mental health-related absences show an increasing trend, highlighting the impact of working conditions on the mental health of nursing professionals and reinforcing the need for preventive measures, mental health promotion strategies, and improvements in workplace conditions.

items.title: Motivation to Use Generative AI at Work: An Expectancy-Value Analysis of a National AI literacy program
items.abstract: AI-literacy training may facilitate workplace adoption of GenAI, yet little is known about how employees’ motivational beliefs change during training. Drawing on expectancy-value theory, we examined motivation before and after Hazlo con IA, a national adaptive AI-literacy program in Chile. The baseline sample included 9,835 working adults across public, healthcare, and small and medium-sized enterprise sectors (SME); 1,864 provided matched pretest–posttest responses. At both time points, attainment value (B = .231–.234), intrinsic value (B = .156–.173), utility value (B = .113–.185), and perceived workplace support (B = .153–.184) positively predicted intentions to use GenAI (all ps < .001). Self-efficacy was positively associated with intentions only at posttest (B = .086, p = .004), whereas perceived costs and anxiety were not significant independent predictors. Following training, all measured constructs except perceived workplace support declined significantly, although effects were small; the largest standardized decline was in intention to use AI (ΔM = −.193, dz = −.29, p < .001). Age (V = .016, p < .001) and employment sector (V = .020, p = .005) showed small multivariate associations with change: older participants reported slightly greater declines in workplace support (B = −.0054), and public-sector employees showed larger declines in intentions than SME employees (ΔM = −.240 vs. −.061, p = .004). Other demographic and experience variables were not significant. These findings highlight the central role of subjective value in workplace GenAI intentions and the relative stability of motivational beliefs across demographic and occupational contexts.

items.title: Motivation to Use Generative AI at Work: An Expectancy-Value Analysis of a National AI literacy program
items.abstract: AI-literacy training may facilitate workplace adoption of GenAI, yet little is known about how employees’ motivational beliefs change during training. Drawing on expectancy-value theory, we examined motivation before and after Hazlo con IA, a national adaptive AI-literacy program in Chile. The baseline sample included 9,835 working adults across public, healthcare, and small and medium-sized enterprise sectors (SME); 1,864 provided matched pretest–posttest responses. At both time points, attainment value (B = .231–.234), intrinsic value (B = .156–.173), utility value (B = .113–.185), and perceived workplace support (B = .153–.184) positively predicted intentions to use GenAI (all ps < .001). Self-efficacy was positively associated with intentions only at posttest (B = .086, p = .004), whereas perceived costs and anxiety were not significant independent predictors. Following training, all measured constructs except perceived workplace support declined significantly, although effects were small; the largest standardized decline was in intention to use AI (ΔM = −.193, dz = −.29, p < .001). Age (V = .016, p < .001) and employment sector (V = .020, p = .005) showed small multivariate associations with change: older participants reported slightly greater declines in workplace support (B = −.0054), and public-sector employees showed larger declines in intentions than SME employees (ΔM = −.240 vs. −.061, p = .004). Other demographic and experience variables were not significant. These findings highlight the central role of subjective value in workplace GenAI intentions and the relative stability of motivational beliefs across demographic and occupational contexts.

items.title: Objectify, Don't Delete: Complaint-Derived Evaluation of Ambient Clinical Notes
items.abstract: Evaluating the quality of AI-generated clinical notes is hard: standard metrics like ROUGE measure lexical similarity to reference notes, while expert checklists encode what committees believe matters. Neither captures what clinicians actually complain about. Recent work has shown that evaluation criteria can be mined from user feedback and filtered to criteria that LLM judges can reliably enforce. We argue that this is where much of the value is lost. The criteria that fail enforceability are disproportionately the ones clinicians raise most often, because high-frequency complaints are stated as several questions glued together. No yes/no judgment can grade such composites as posed. We introduce an objectification step that rewrites such criteria into sets of scoped, determinate decisions. We demonstrate the approach through an evaluation pipeline that mines criteria from complaints, objectifies them, and deploys LLM judges against both planted defects and production notes. Across eleven defects planted into ACI-bench reference notes, objectified judges localize violations with median recall of 0.95, while reference metrics change by at most 0.037. Given the complaint as one broad question, the same judges still find every planted defect, but they also flag 70% of the unperturbed reference notes; one section-pair question per call raises Youden's J from 0.30 to 0.72 (by 0.19 to 0.26 with prompt effort matched). We release ACI-Defect, a perturbation benchmark; clinician-reviewed instance-level labels showing quality gaps in the ACI-bench gold standard (32 of 40 notes contain hallucinations; 40 of 40 omit discussed facts); and grounding-judge verdicts. On 1,446 production notes, mean instance-rate burden falls at every clinician-rating step (rho=-0.15), a small association. Defect counts have to be kept per span rather than collapsed into one pass/fail bit per note.

items.title: Öğrenci Eyleyiciliği Ölçeği'nin Geliştirilmesi
items.abstract: Bu araştırmanın amacı, üniversite öğrencilerinin öğrenci eyleyiciliği düzeylerini belirlemeye yönelik geçerli ve güvenilir bir ölçme aracı olan Öğrenci Eyleyiciliği Ölçeği'ni geliştirmektir. Türkiye'de geliştirilen öğrenci katılımı ölçeklerinin eyleyiciliği bağımsız ve bütüncül bir yapı olarak ele almaması, çalışmanın temel gerekçesini oluşturmaktadır. Metodolojik nitelikteki araştırmada, alanyazına dayalı olarak oluşturulan 128 maddelik madde havuzu üç uzmanın görüşüne sunulmuş; uzman görüşleri doğrultusunda 46 madde çıkarılmış, 6 madde yeniden ifade edilmiş ve 82 maddelik beşli Likert tipi taslak form elde edilmiştir. Taslak form 440 üniversite öğrencisine uygulanmış, 146 form değerlendirme dışı bırakılmış ve kalan 294 form seçkisiz olarak birbirinden bağımsız iki gruba ayrılmıştır. Birinci grupta (n = 143) açımlayıcı faktör analizi, ikinci grupta (n = 151) doğrulayıcı faktör analizi yürütülmüştür. Verilerin faktörleşmeye uygunluğu KMO (.82) ve Bartlett testiyle doğrulanmıştır. Paralel analiz ve açımlayıcı faktör analizi sonucunda toplam varyansın %36.6'sını açıklayan, 25 maddelik üç faktörlü bir yapı elde edilmiştir. Doğrulayıcı faktör analizinde 72. madde çıkarılmış ve 24 maddelik nihai model sınırda bir uyum göstermiştir (χ²/sd = 1.72; RMSEA = .069; SRMR = .067; CFI = .859; TLI = .844). Ölçek, üretken inisiyatif ve yaratıcılık, öz-düzenleme ve sorumluluk ile yardım arama ve öğretmen etkileşimi boyutlarından oluşmaktadır. Boyutlara ilişkin Cronbach alfa katsayıları .76 ile .89 arasında, ölçeğin tamamı için .91 olarak hesaplanmıştır. Bununla birlikte öz-düzenleme ve sorumluluk boyutunda ortalama açıklanan varyans düşük kalmış, üretken inisiyatif ile öz-düzenleme boyutları arasındaki yüksek korelasyon (r = .76) ayırt edici geçerliliği sınırlamış; Fornell–Larcker ölçütü diğer iki boyut çiftinde de karşılanmamıştır. Sonuç olarak ölçeğin yeterli güvenilirliğe sahip olduğu, ancak yapı geçerliliğine ilişkin kanıtların sınırda kaldığı ve yapının bağımsız, daha büyük örneklemlerde ikinci düzey ve iki faktörlü modellerle yeniden sınanması gerektiği belirlenmiştir.
